reviews.text:
I have visited many McDonald’s locations, but unfortunately, my experience at the Times Square location was the worst I’ve ever had.

It was early in the morning, and I just wanted a quick breakfast. I ordered my food and went upstairs to eat. A few minutes later, my fiancée began to feel unwell, so I quickly stepped out to a nearby pharmacy to get her some medication. When I returned just a few minutes later, a security guard stopped me and asked if I had ordered food. I explained that I had already ordered and had the receipt, but I needed a moment to find it.

Instead of listening, he repeatedly asked if I was going to order and kept pointing at the kiosk. It seemed like he did not understand what I was saying. I calmly told him, “Sir, you’re not listening to me,” but he then got angry, and again, pointed to a sign about the 30-minute limit time, which was not relevant to the situation. I was simply trying to explain that I had a brief emergency and needed to step out for a few minutes.

All of this happened while I was searching for my receipt, and I was not given the chance to calmly find it. Once I showed the receipt, he allowed me upstairs without saying anything and simply pointed toward the stairs.

The entire situation felt unnecessary and could have been avoided with better communication. I understand that Times Square is very busy, and I respect that rules need to be enforced. However, a little patience and basic communication would have made a big difference.

I simply wanted to enjoy a quick breakfast and leave. Emergencies do happen, and customers should be treated with understanding and professionalism in those moments.

God forbid if you ever have an emergency, because if you do, this security guard will give you a harder time than what you already have.
reviews.author: WarriorOfPeace

Waited 30 minutes for a cone ice cream despite following up twice — unacceptable service.
I ordered a cone through the self-service kiosk at 8:44 PM. No receipt was printed, but I waited near the counter assuming the order was in the system.
By 9:05 PM, after waiting over 20 minutes, nothing had been prepared. I saw other customers receive assistance after speaking with staff, so I approached a male staff member and explained that I had been waiting since 8:44. He said he would check.
By 9:14 PM, my order still had not come out. I returned again, showed my card payment history, and explained that I had now been waiting 30 minutes for an ice cream. Only then did he contact the ice cream station, and I finally received my order.
The staff member did not hand me the item himself and asked another employee to do so.
This was not an issue of the store being busy. An ice cream taking 30 minutes with multiple follow-ups reflects poor communication and inadequate customer service.

reviews.text:
I had a really disappointing experience at this location. First of all, the setup doesn’t work for the volume of people coming through — it’s in the middle of Times Square but completely unprepared for the crowds. There was no system in place to manage lines or assist customers, and the few employees behind the counter were overwhelmed and unresponsive to questions, directing everyone to the self-serve kiosks.

The food was subpar: stale fries, chewy chicken nuggets, no ice, and no ketchup or sauces available. To make it worse, no napkins were stocked, and the bathroom had no soap. Basic things like cleanliness, condiments, and customer service were just missing entirely.

If you’re in the area, I’d recommend avoid this spot.

I am a loyal and frequent customer of this location and visit nearly every morning. The treatment I received was unacceptable.

On December 25, 2025, I placed an online order for pickup at Restaurant 39148. When I arrived, the restaurant was closed due to Christmas. I fully understand holiday closures. However, the online ordering system did not indicate that this location was closed or unavailable for pickup, resulting in payment for an order I could not receive.

I returned the following morning to retrieve my order or request a refund. Instead of assistance, I was met with hostility and accusations of dishonesty from the managers on duty. I was told I was lying because they claimed no orders were received the prior day. Even after presenting clear proof of purchase and payment from my debit card, I continued to be treated as though I was attempting to defraud the company.

One manager walked away from the register in visible frustration before completing my order. Another manager’s demeanor implied that I was stealing from the brand. The tone set by management caused the entire staff to treat me with suspicion. I was humiliated and discredited in front of others, despite being a daily customer of this location.

I clearly stated that I was willing to accept a refund. My concern is not the food but the conduct. Accusing a customer of dishonesty, disregarding documented proof, and responding with contempt reflects a serious failure in leadership and customer service.

McDonald’s is a respected global brand, and this experience fell far below its standards. I am requesting a review of this incident and appropriate corrective action to ensure customers are treated with professionalism and respect.

The food was great, and the service was exceptional—exactly what you’d expect from a global brand. However, something in the store left me shocked and deeply hurt.

On the wall map, Kashmir was shown as part of another country. I want to ask—who designed or approved this map? How can such a serious misrepresentation be displayed so casually in a global outlet?

Let me be clear:
Kashmir was a part of India, is a part of India, and will always be a part of India.

This kind of error is not just incorrect—it’s offensive and disrespectful to the sovereignty and sentiments of millions of Indians. I urge McDonald’s global management to take immediate action to correct the map and ensure this does not happen again. As a global brand, you have a responsibility to be accurate and sensitive to geopolitical realities.

Please treat this issue with the seriousness it deserves.

Today is my birthday, and I came to dine with my friends. When I returned from the restroom, I discovered that my order was missing both the ice cream and the drink. I went to the counter to report the issue. After returning to my seat and opening my burger, I found that the Chicken Mac I ordered had been replaced with a beef burger. I do not eat beef, so I immediately went back to the counter. I showed the staff my receipt and the opened burger, clearly explaining that I ordered a Chicken Mac and was given a beef burger.

What happened next was absolutely unacceptable. The staff member looked directly at the beef burger in my hand and insisted, “This is the chicken burger.” I had to hold back my anger and told her again, “This is a beef burger.” It is unbelievable that an employee at McDonald’s cannot tell the difference between a fried chicken patty and a beef patty.

It only became even more ridiculous when another employee walked by and the staff member stopped her to ask, while pointing at my burger, “Is this a chicken burger?” The other employee immediately replied, “That’s a beef burger,” and replaced it with the correct order. This clearly shows that the initial staff member had no idea what she was talking about.

This is a serious issue with employee training. If she wasn’t sure, she should have confirmed with another staff member instead of confidently giving wrong information. And frankly, it is shocking that McDonald’s employees would need to be reminded of something as basic as distinguishing chicken from beef. I never expected that I would have to point out such a fundamental mistake. It completely ruined my birthday dining experience.
